title: Can rotated squares beat axis-parallel packings

problemStatement.formal: rotationHelps : Prop := exists n, f_rot n > g_ap n
problemStatement.plain: Does there exist n such that allowing rotation strictly improves the maximum total side-length sum when packing n squares in [0,1]^2?
whyMatters: Resolves the gap between BKU axis-parallel result and the full Erdos conjecture
If rotation never helps, the general conjecture follows from BKU

proven: f_rot(k^2) = g(k^2) = k for all k >= 1 (Cauchy-Schwarz tightness)
open: Is f_rot(n) = g(n) for all n?
Can diamond tiling of rotated squares ever be more efficient?
knownResults.goal: Determine whether rotation ever helps in square packing

currentState.focus: Axiom elimination: 8→6 axioms via geometric side bound and sSup reasoning
currentState.nextAction: Docker build verification when Docker available

knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS: Eliminated 2 axioms (g_ap_bounded, f_rot_perfect_square → theorems). Proved side_le_sqrt_two, g_ap_le_f_rot, BddAbove. 8→6 axioms, 0→1 sorry (trivial: packing existence).
builtItems: Created proofs/Proofs/Erdos106OQ02.lean (219 lines, 11 theorems, 8 axioms, 0 sorries)
RotatedSquare structure with center, side, angle; interior via inverse rotation
GeneralPacking and AxisParallelPacking structures with containment/disjointness
f_rot(n) and g_ap(n) objective functions as suprema
Gallery entry: src/data/proofs/erdos-106-oq-02/ with meta.json, annotations.json, index.ts
side_le_sqrt_two theorem: s ≤ √2 for contained rotated squares
midpoint_*_mem_closure lemmas (4): edge midpoints are in closure
f_rot_set_bddAbove: BddAbove for general packing sum set
insights: Rotation preserves area, so Cauchy-Schwarz bound f_rot(n) <= sqrt(n) still holds
At perfect squares k^2, both f_rot and g_ap equal k — rotation cannot help at these values
The general Erdos conjecture decomposes as (rotation never helps) + BKU
No example is known where rotation helps; the first unresolved case is f_rot(10) vs g(10)
f_rot(2) = 1 follows from the original Erdos argument for both rotated and axis-parallel squares
g_ap_bounded follows from f_rot_bounded via g_ap ≤ f_rot (AP packings are general packings)
f_rot_perfect_square follows from g_ap_perfect_square + f_rot_bounded + g_ap ≤ f_rot
side_le_sqrt_two: contained rotated squares have side ≤ √2 — proved from edge midpoint containment + s²cos²θ + s²sin²θ ≤ 2
The g_ap_set_nonempty sorry (existence of a packing) is trivially true but requires explicit Lean construction of n tiny squares
nextSteps: Verify compilation when Docker is available
Attempt to prove f_rot(2) = 1 from first principles instead of axiomatizing
Investigate if area argument alone can prove g(n) <= f_rot(n) formally in Lean
Consider creating Aristotle companion file for routine lemmas
